summary.text: An exoplanet, or extrasolar planet, is a planet outside the Solar System.
The first confirmed detection came in 1992 around a pulsar, and by November 2026 there were 6,464 confirmed exoplanets.
Transit photometry and Doppler spectroscopy have found the most, but both favor spotting large planets close to their star.

facts.label: Lightest known
facts.value: Draugr, about twice the Moon's mass

facts.label: Sun-like star odds
facts.value: About 1 in 5 estimated to have an Earth-sized habitable-zone planet

items.prompt: A friend asks which star hosts the nearest known planets outside our Solar System.

options.label: Sirius, the brightest star in our night sky
Betelgeuse, a huge red star in Orion
Polaris, the star that marks north
Proxima Centauri, the Sun's closest star

items.explain: The nearest exoplanets orbit Proxima Centauri, the closest star to the Sun.

items.prompt: Most planets found so far are large and sit close to their stars. What is the best explanation?

options.label: The main detection methods favor spotting such planets
Small planets far from stars are unable to form
Large close-in planets are the only kind that exist
Stars with small planets are too dim to observe

items.explain: The two most productive methods are biased toward large planets close to the star, so the known list leans that way.

items.prompt: An object orbiting a star is well above the mass where deuterium fusion starts. Under the main mass-based definition, what is it?

options.label: A planet, because it orbits a star
A brown dwarf, because it is above the limit
A rogue planet, because it is so heavy
A moon, because the star dwarfs it

items.explain: Substellar objects above the deuterium-fusion mass limit are brown dwarfs, wherever they are and however they formed.

items.prompt: Two exoplanets are known: one circles its star in under an hour, another takes thousands of years. What most likely differs?

options.label: The first is far more massive than the second
The first is far younger than the second
The first sits far closer to its star than the second
The first is far brighter than the second

items.explain: Orbital times run from under an hour for planets closest to their star to thousands of years for the farthest.

items.prompt: Astronomers give special attention to planets in a star's goldilocks zone. Why?

options.label: Such planets are always the largest ones
Such planets are the easiest to photograph
Such planets are the nearest to Earth
Liquid water could exist on their surface

items.explain: In that zone liquid water, a prerequisite for life as we know it, could exist on the surface.

items.prompt: A team finds an object just under the 13-Jupiter-mass line that is fusing some deuterium. What does that say about the line?

options.label: It is a rough guide, not a precise physical boundary
It is a strict law that this object has broken
It proves the object is really a brown dwarf
It shows the line should be moved to 5 Jupiter masses

items.explain: Deuterium fusion can occur in some objects below the cutoff, so the 13-Jupiter-mass limit has no precise physical significance.
